best_for: Developers on Windows or a Mac who spend the day in a terminal and want SSH sessions, file previews, an editor and an AI assistant side by side, without signing up for anything.
description:
Wave is an open-source terminal app, released under the Apache-2.0 license, that puts files, notes, web pages and AI chat next to your command line. Its makers build it in the open on GitHub.

SSH sessions in Wave survive a dropped connection, a network change or a restart of the app, and reconnect on their own. Any block, such as a terminal or a preview, can go full screen with one click and come back just as fast. The `wsh` command lets you run the workspace from the shell, for example copying files between your computer and a remote server with `wsh file`. You can store API keys in your system's own secure storage, build dashboards from widgets, and share layouts with coworkers.

points.title: Open source, no account
points.text: Wave is Apache-2.0 software that needs no login or account, and it keeps your data on your machine.

points.title: Terminal, editor and browser in one window
points.text: You split the window into terminals, a code editor with syntax highlighting, and web views, and save layouts as workspaces. Files such as images, Markdown, CSV and video preview inline, and an SSH connection manager switches between servers and WSL.

points.title: The built-in AI wants telemetry on
points.text: Wave AI reads terminal output and can work on files. Its default setup normally requires telemetry. If you set your own key or a local model as the default, that requirement goes away. Presets cover OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, Gemini and Azure OpenAI, and local models run through Ollama, LM Studio or vLLM.

points.title: What telemetry sends and how to stop it
points.text: It sends system details, app version, feature use and AI token counts under a random ID, but never your prompts, replies or hostnames. You can switch it off on the welcome screen or with `wsh setconfig telemetry:enabled=false`, and the separate ping with the `WAVETERM_NOPING` variable.

points.title: Windows build is a single x64 MSI
points.text: The project asks for Windows 10 1809 or later on x64, and this listing has one x64 MSI per release. The Windows listing keeps 13 versions, back to 0.8.12.

points.title: Linux exists, but not in this listing
points.text: Linux builds for x64 and Arm64 need glibc 2.28 or later, which means Debian 10, RHEL 8 or Ubuntu 20.04 and up. They come as Snap, AppImage, .deb, .rpm, zip and pacman packages from the project's site.

points.title: Mac builds for both chips, current release only
points.text: macOS has separate DMGs for Intel and Apple silicon. Only the current release, 0.14.5, is listed for the Mac.
